 The quick turnaround will involve precision coordination. Share Atlanta Dream fans cheer before Game 3 of the WNBA Finals game against Golden State Valkyries at State Farm Arena on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, in Atlanta. (Hyosub Shin/AJC) By Lauren Williams Oct 24, 2026 State Farm Arena has had a busy schedule in October. 
 But it comes to a head on Saturday, when the arena team has to flip courts from the Dream’s Game 4 WNBA Finals matchup against the Valkyries to the Hawks’ home opener against the Rockets.
 Typically, the arena crew has about five to six hours to convert to different configurations. But on Saturday, the crew will have just a few hours.
 On average, Dream games last about 2.5 hours.
 “We’re estimating the end time (of the Dream game) to be somewhere around 3:30 or 4, and then we’re opening doors again at 7:30,” Amanda Mann, State Farm Arena’s executive vice president and chief facilities officer, said.
